source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Andropogon gerardii and variety key, printed p.550
source_material: Owner supplied printed p.550 species account and three-variety key. Partial facing-page distribution and neighboring species are not assigned to this record; no scans/figures republished.

option.label: Sessile FIRST glume concave, with two keels
option.detail: Inspect the first outer glume of the stalkless spikelet. Gould calls it concave and two-keeled. Two keels do not establish two veins, and concavity is not a glandular pit or proof of hairlessness.

option_additions.subgroup: First glume: sessile versus stalked spikelet

option.label: Sessile SECOND glume has one keel
option.detail: Locate the second outer glume. Gould says single-keeled; one keel is NOT evidence of one vein.

option_additions.subgroup: First glume: sessile versus stalked spikelet

option.label: LOWER lemma thin and mostly translucent
option.detail: Open one spikelet and locate the lower inner lemma, not a glume. Gould calls it thin and mostly hyaline. This is not the upper fertile lemma.

option.label: UPPER lemma deeply two-lobed
option.detail: Inspect the upper fertile lemma: Gould describes two deep lobes with the awn arising from between them. Do not transfer the lobes to a glume.

option.label: Awn emerges between upper lemma lobes
option.detail: Trace a real awn to the notch between the upper fertile lemma lobes; the lower lemma is separately thin/hyaline.

option.label: Lower segment of lemma awn twisted
option.detail: Inspect the awn below its free upper portion. Gould describes twisting below; this alone does not establish a bent/kneed awn.

option.label: Hair tuft at FLOWERING rachis node
option.detail: Find a node of the flowering branch rachis, not a culm joint or floret callus. Gould reports a tuft of hairs at these rachis nodes.

option.label: Stalked companion spikelet about as large
option.detail: Compare a sessile spikelet and its attached pedicelled companion. Gould describes a usually equally large, awnless staminate companion, not a rudimentary stalk-only partner.

option.label: Well-developed rhizomes
option.detail: Confirm attached underground stems. Gould reports developed rhizomes in historical var. chrysocomus and var. paucipilus; var. gerardii can have short or absent rhizomes. This does not prove every tuft has long scaly runners.

option.label: Copious golden rachis-joint hairs, about 3–5 mm
option.detail: Measure hairs on flowering rachis INTERNODES. Gould assigns copious usually yellow/golden 3–5 mm hairs to historical var. chrysocomus; other varieties differ. Not hairs on culm nodes or glumes.

evidence.note: Gould gives blades mostly 5–10 mm broad. The approximate narrow band includes the 5-mm boundary; medium is supported. Retain H&L 2–10 mm range separately.

evidence.note: Species account: awn arises between two upper-lemma lobes and twists below. Variety key permits awnless or short-awned sessile spikelets in var. paucipilus, rarely >5 mm; var. gerardii has 8–20 mm awns. Pedicelled staminate spikelet awnless. Short fertile awns are source-permitted; no universal absence or invented 1–1.5-mm species limit.

evidence.note: Species flowering rachis internodes ciliate with usually long hairs, rachis nodes with a hair tuft. Var. chrysocomus: copious usually golden/yellow hairs 3–5 mm. Var. gerardii: sparse to copious mostly 1–2 mm hairs. Var. paucipilus: variable typically short sparse internode hairs. None of these are automatically culm-node or glume hairs.

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Measure a sessile spikelet and compare its companion
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould gives sessile spikelets 7–11 mm, with a staminate awnless pedicelled companion usually about as large. The first glume is concave and two-keeled; the second has one keel and is equally long.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: KR Gould sessile spikelets are 3–4.5 mm. Measure an actual spikelet, not the awn or entire flowering branch; current size context is not a new exclusion button.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Exact source comparison, not a local voucher or automatic exclusion from head shape.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Andropogon gerardii and variety key, printed p.550

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Inspect both lemmas and the awn attachment
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: The lower lemma is thin and mostly hyaline. The upper is deeply two-lobed with an awn between lobes, twisted below. Big bluestem cannot be universally rejected for a short or absent awn: Gould var. paucipilus permits those states.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: Twisted below is not enough to claim bent AND twisted. The awnless stalked companion is a different spikelet from a short-awned or awnless sessile floret.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Gould p.550 variety distinctions retained; no assumed exact 1–1.5-mm limit.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Andropogon gerardii and variety key, printed p.550

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Keep flowering-axis hairs and rhizomes tied to the variety
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould var. chrysocomus has copious usually golden 3–5 mm rachis-internode hairs and developed rhizomes; var. gerardii has mostly 1–2 mm hairs and absent/short rhizomes; var. paucipilus has typically short sparse variable hairs and developed rhizomes. Rachis nodes have hair tufts, separate from culm nodes.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: Diggs uses two subspecies and treats chrysocomus as a hybrid, so the two books are not a one-to-one variety map. Do not combine all variety characters as a required description of one plant.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Historical variety key and later subspecies concepts preserved separately.

secondary_reference_review.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O’Kennon (1999), Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
secondary_reference_review.access: Directly read owner-connected reference PDF text
secondary_reference_review.corroborates: 2–7 digitate branches, 4–11 cm; large 7–11 mm sessile and comparable awnless pedicellate spikelets; awned/awnless variation; membranous ligules.
secondary_reference_review.taxon_caution: Diggs includes historical var. paucipilus in subsp. hallii and describes chrysocomus as a hybrid of the two subspecies. Do not collapse Gould three-variety key into a one-to-one Diggs subspecies mapping. Source ranges remain alongside, not merged into one compulsory interval.

non_scoring_context.culms: glabrous, often glaucous; not evidence of hairless culm nodes
non_scoring_context.distribution: Partial facing-page continuation not transcribed; no county nativity inference.

omissions_not_absences: No ordinary culm-node hair state inferred from flowering rachis-node tufts.
No first-glume vein count inferred from two keels; no upper one-vein state from a single keel.
No bent/kneed awn inferred solely from lower-segment twisting.
No universal rhizome presence or absence.
No full-variety identity or local specimen certification.
